full_judgment:
2. The short facts leading to the case is that the petitioners as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No. 81 of 1995 in the Court of Joint District Judge, Second Court, Mymensingh against the opposite parties as defendants praying for decree of declaration of title and recovery of khas possession of the suit land as described in the plaint of the suit. The opposite parties as defendants contested the suit by filing written statement denying the allegations made in the plaint and prayed for dismissal of the suit. The trial court after framing issues, hearing the parties and perusing the evidence on record decreed the suit by judgment and decree dated 29.11.1999. The opposite-parties being aggrieved preferred Title Appeal No.27 of 2000 before the District Judge, Mymensingh which on transfer was heard and disposed of by the Additional District Judge, Mymensingh and by his judgment and decree dated 13.03.2003 allowing the appeal dismissed the suit setting aside the judgment and decree passed by the trial court. 

 10. In the instant case the petitioners were fully depended on their. Tadbirkar and for his negligence the said delay of 1428 days was caused in preferring the civil revision against the impugned judgment and decree. It appears to me that the delay caused was not for the fault of the petitioners rather it was due to Tadbirkar of the petitioners. For that reasons the petitioners should not suffer inasmuch as the door of justice should not shut out to them. The petitioners instituted the suit for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession and accordingly they should get a chance to agitate their grievance before this court. Further the opposite parties also do not have any objection if the delay is condoned.
